title: An ironworks firm was released in 2024: had the $750,000 settlement been paid in full?

beats.text: March 2021: the City suspends Kwan Wo Ironworks, and its owner.

visual.text: KWAN WO IRONWORKS INC., a California corporation: suspended

beats.text: By December 2024, the firm is on Public Works contracts again.

visual.toLab: on a Public Works contract team

beats.text: The City cleared it in April 2024. Had it paid its 750,000 dollar settlement?
This is a lead, not a finding.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: In 2020 the owner was charged in the Public Works bribery cases.
The U.S. Attorney says she owns Kwan Wo Ironworks.

visual.line: a construction company called Kwan Wo Ironworks

beats.text: She pleaded guilty to bribing the Public Works director. Then prison, and a 95,000 dollar fine.

visual.label: fine
visual.sub: and one year and one day in prison, 11 February 2021

beats.text: The first lead. Six City reports, 2021 to 2023, list the firm as suspended.

visual.text: KWAN WO IRONWORKS INC., a California corporation: “Issued and effective on 3/1/2021, no hearing or end date identified yet.”

beats.text: Issued and effective on 3/1/2021, no hearing or end date identified yet.

visual.line: no hearing or end date identified yet

beats.text: In 2024, the City Attorney announced a 750,000 dollar settlement with her and affiliates.

visual.label: settlement with the owner and affiliates

beats.text: The second lead. From 2024 the entry reads: debarred for 5 years, to March 2026.

visual.text: …, Kin Wo Construction, Inc. and SFR Recovery, Inc. · debarred · 5 years · end date 3/1/2026

beats.text: It names Kin Wo Construction, another of her companies, which the settlement debars.

visual.kicker: Two companies: the settlement debars the first

beats.text: The City Attorney’s letter says: from April 24, 2024, the ironworks firm was free to work.

visual.kicker: City Attorney to the Controller, 20 June 2024
visual.text: “As of April 24, 2024, Kwan Wo Ironworks is not suspended and is free to do business with the City”

beats.text: But the Board’s resolution kept it suspended until full payment of 750,000 dollars.

visual.line: until full payment of the settlement amount of $750,000

beats.text: The settlement gave until March 2026 for the last 350,000.
Was all of it paid by April 2024? The payment records are not on file.

visual.label: Paid in full by 24 April 2024?
visual.sub: the payment records are not on file

beats.text: Its own wording may let the firm back after the first 400,000 dollars.

visual.line: until payment in full of the Settlement Payment or until March 1, 2024, whichever comes later

beats.text: The third lead: four Public Works contracts list the firm. 3.4 million dollars agreed.

visual.label: agreed to the firm as a subcontractor

beats.text: 452,237 dollars is recorded as paid so far.
Nuru extended an Animal Care and Control bidding deadline for her other firm. Is ACC that building?

visual.label: Is “SF ACC” that building?
visual.sub: contract 1000035556, “PW SF ACC TENANT IMPR”; the memo also says the owner helped install an iron fence at Nuru’s ranch

beats.text: The largest, Portsmouth Square, began in February 2026.
All four began after the release, the first eight months later.

visual.kicker: All four began after the release

beats.text: Of 33 firms on the City’s reports that were tested, it is the only one.

visual.line: Of 33 firms on the City’s reports that were tested, this is the only one

beats.text: The fourth lead. 44 days after the charge, the owner left the State licence.
That can be a real change of ownership, or only a change of names.

visual.line: a real change of ownership, or only a change of names

beats.text: Who owns it now, the files do not show.
A prime contractor picks its subcontractors, and the table dates the contract, not them.

visual.label: A prime contractor picks its subcontractors
visual.sub: the table records the day a contract began

beats.text: What would settle it? The City’s record of when the 750,000 dollars was paid.

cards.what: The City’s record of the settlement payments: the dates of the $400,000 and $350,000
Subcontractor lists and approval dates for the four contracts

beats.text: No authority has made a finding about the release or the four contracts.
A lead is a question, not an accusation.
